final.title: The real limit of dual running
final.body:
Dual running looks simple until you treat it as an actual workflow decision. For an owner-operator, it means keeping the manual process in place while a new AI-assisted path runs beside it. That only makes sense for one repeatable workflow where you are weighing manual labour, another hire, or automation.

The limit is overlap. While both paths exist, someone has to compare outputs, resolve differences, and decide which path is the source of truth. That is a control the owner sets, not a magic trick. And for money movement or other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory.

Bareni’s normal sequence is straightforward: identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, then define a small working MVP, fixed scope, and measures. That is method, not a promise of results. The point of dual running is not to admire two systems forever; it is to learn whether the new path can carry the load before the old one is switched off.

A practical next step is to ask yourself: how much owner time goes into this workflow each week, and how many decision points genuinely need your judgment? If the answer is many, overlap will be hard to justify. If it is narrow, a short pilot can show whether the new system is worth keeping.
